title: reading a compile-time asset adds no runtime platform requirement, so a function that reads one still satisfies a native pin
notes: docs/ASSET_LOADERS.md (Locked): 'Loading happens during compilation. It does not add `FileSystem` or another runtime platform requirement to the importing program.' docs/src/pages/guide/asset-imports.mdx: 'There is no runtime file path to deploy.' specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin': 'A native pin MUST be a checked assertion over the complete transitive graph. Compilation MUST fail if any reachable operation or provider requires TypeScript.' That makes the pin the observation channel for the asset rule: if the compiler-issued asset module were charged as a runtime TypeScript dependency, SMITHERS3001 would name it here. The pin spelling is the provisional `native(fn)` area 21 uses; the rule it observes is spelling-independent. RETIRED MARKERS (js and go, 2026-08-23): the reference used to charge the built-in `TypeScript` requirement for the asset edge and reject the pin with SMITHERS3001, because `poc/src/targets/classify.ts`'s portability pass never learned which relative imports the source-asset stage owns; the fork reached the same SMITHERS3001 by the other route, having no source-asset stage at all (observed SMITHERS1506@10:13, SMITHERS1506@10:28, SMITHERS1510@2:20, SMITHERS3001@13:1). Both are fixed: the reference exempts compile-time asset edges from the requirement and the fork has a source-asset stage. `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --backend both --jobs 4` scored this case XPASS on BOTH backends and both now print `production/2`. This is the only row that would notice a compile-time constant becoming a runtime platform dependency again.
